ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: mod dependency has no download link
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A mod lists another mod as a dependency but did not add a download or Workshop link for it. This is harmless. The game still runs and nothing is broken.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Nothing to fix in your game. If you made the named mod, add a steamWorkshopUrl and/or downloadUrl to that dependency in its About.xml. Otherwise you can safely ignore this.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: mod has an invalid packageId
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A mod's packageId is not in the expected author.modname format (letters, numbers and dots). The game still loads it, but a malformed packageId can confuse dependency and load-order checks.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: An authoring issue in the named mod. If it is yours, set a valid packageId like yourname.modname in About.xml. Otherwise report it to the author; it is usually safe to ignore.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: mod dependency metadata is incomplete
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A mod's About.xml has a dependency entry that is incomplete: a missing packageId, an invalid packageId, or an empty display name. Harmless to play, but the dependency may not resolve correctly.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: An authoring issue in the named mod. If it is yours, fill in the dependency's packageId and displayName. Otherwise ignore it or report it to the author.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: null reference exception
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A piece of code tried to use something that did not exist (a null value). This is the most common error type and usually means a mod ran into a situation its author did not expect.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Check the likely source above. If it names a mod, that mod probably needs an update or is conflicting with another. Disable it to confirm, then send the author the full stack trace.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: missing method or member
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: Code called a method or field that does not exist in the version that is loaded. This almost always means two mods expect different versions of the same code, or a mod was built against a different game or library version than you have.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Make sure the game, the named mod, and Harmony are all up to date. If the trace mentions another mod's type, a version mismatch between those two mods is the likely cause. Update or remove the older one.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a mod failed to load its code
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A mod's assembly could not be loaded fully. Every feature from that mod is disabled and its defs may fail to load, which often cascades into many more errors.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: This usually means a missing dependency or a version conflict. Confirm the named mod's required mods are installed and active, that load order is correct, and that Harmony is present and up to date.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: missing texture
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: The game tried to load an image that is not there. The item, pawn, or UI element that needs it will show a pink and black placeholder.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: The named mod is missing a texture or points at the wrong path. If you renamed or moved files, undo that; otherwise reinstall the mod. If it only happens with another mod active, a patch is pointing at a texture that does not exist.

keywords.li: failed to find any textures at

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: missing sound
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: The game tried to load a sound file that is not present. The sound simply will not play.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: The named mod is missing an audio file or references the wrong path. Reinstall the mod, or report the missing path to its author.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a mod's startup code threw an error
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A mod's start-of-game initialization (a static constructor) threw an exception, so part or all of that mod is left half set up. This often breaks one feature while the rest of the mod appears to work.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Find the mod named in the message or trace, update it, and confirm its required mods are active and in the right order. If it started right after a game update, the mod likely needs a version bump. Report the trace to the author.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a def shortcut was used too early
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A mod read a DefOf (a code shortcut to a specific def) before defs finished loading, so the value was empty. This is a startup-timing bug in the mod, and the feature that needed the def will not work.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: An author-side timing bug in the named mod; update it. If it only appears alongside another mod, a load-order or patch conflict is exposing it. Report the exact message to the author.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a def's validation code threw
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: While checking a def for problems, the game's validation code itself threw an exception. The def is often built anyway, but the error hides whatever real problem the check was trying to report.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: A bug in the mod that owns the named def or patch, sometimes exposed by another mod changing shared data. Update the mod, check its dependencies, and report the message if it persists.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: unresolved def reference
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A def refers to another def by name that does not exist. The referring content is broken or missing until the reference resolves.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: A required mod is probably missing or loads after the mod that needs it. Confirm all dependencies of the named mod are installed and active, and fix load order so the mod providing the referenced def loads first.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: unknown type in XML
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A def or patch names a C# class that is not loaded, so RimWorld cannot build that def and the content it defines will not appear.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: The mod that provides that class is missing or failed to load, or a soft dependency is not installed. Install the required mod. If the class belongs to the named mod itself, its code did not load, so look for an earlier assembly load error.

keywords.li: could not find a type named

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: unknown XML field
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A def or patch sets a field that does not exist on that type, so the value is ignored and the intended effect is missing.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: A bug in the named mod's XML, often from a game update that renamed or removed the field, or a patch aimed at the wrong type. Update the mod or report it to the author.

keywords.li: corresponds to a field in type

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: duplicate defName
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: Two defs share the same name, so RimWorld keeps only one and the other is silently overridden. This can make a mod behave as if a feature is missing.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Two mods define the same thing, or a patch adds a def that already exists. This is usually a mod conflict; report both mod names to the authors, or remove one.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: XML error in a mod
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A mod's XML is malformed or uses a field the game does not recognise, so the affected def or patch is skipped.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: This is a bug in the named mod's data files. If you edited any XML, revert it. Otherwise report the exact message to the mod author; there is nothing to fix on your end.

keywords.li: could not load defs for mod

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a mod's custom XML failed to load
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A mod uses its own code to read one of its XML nodes, and that code threw, so the value is skipped and the content that needed it is missing or misconfigured.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: A bug in the named mod's XML or its loader code, often after a game update changed the expected shape. Update the mod, revert any hand-edited XML, and report the message to the author.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: missing translation key
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A translation problem: the game had no active language for a lookup, a translated string blew up while formatting its arguments, or the active language's translation files contain errors. A simple missing key never logs anything - the game silently falls back to English.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Harmless to play. The formatting variant means a translation has the wrong number of {0} placeholders for its arguments. For the file-error count, open the translation report (Options - generate translation report) to see which key or field is at fault, then tell that language pack's author.

keywords.li: generate translation report for more info

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a patch could not apply
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A mod's XML patch did not apply, usually because its target no longer exists or another mod changed it first, so the patched change did not happen.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Often a load-order or compatibility issue between the named mod and another. Update the mod, adjust load order, or report the patch failure to the author.

keywords.li: failed to find a node with the given xpath

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: could not load a saved reference
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: While loading, the game could not find something it referenced by name. In a save this usually means a mod that was present before is now missing or changed.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: If this happened loading a save, a mod was removed or updated since the save was made. Re-add the missing mod, or accept that the referenced content is gone. At startup it points to a missing dependency or a load-order problem.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a saved object reference could not be found
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: While loading a save, the game could not find an object another object pointed at by its saved id. The thing was removed, not saved correctly, or belonged to a mod that is no longer present, so the reference is dropped.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Usually a mod was removed or changed since the save was made. Re-add the missing mod to recover the content, or accept that the referenced object is gone. On a fresh game it points to a mod bug; report the trace to the mod in the likely source.

keywords.li: could not resolve reference to object with loadid

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: save is from a different game version
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: You loaded a save, config, or mod list created on a different RimWorld version than you are running now. Within the same major version this is usually fine; across major versions some content may not load cleanly.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Nothing to fix if the game plays normally. If follow-on errors appear, the save predates a game or mod update: match your RimWorld and mod versions to those the save was made with, or start a new colony on the current version.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a loading step threw an error
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: Code running during a loading screen (a long event, such as generating a map or loading a save) threw an exception. Whatever that step was setting up may be incomplete, which can cascade into later errors.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Look at the likely source and trace for the mod driving that step. Update or disable it, confirm its dependencies are active, and report the trace to the author.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: raid used a default arrival mode
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: The game could not pick an arrival mode for a raid, so it sent the raiders in on foot from the map edge instead. This happens when none of the arrival modes allowed by that raid strategy can be used with this particular faction and map - for example when a faction cannot use drop pods, or a raid strategy lists arrival modes that do not fit the situation. The raid itself still runs normally; only how the attackers arrive changed.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Nothing is broken and no action is needed - the raid went ahead. If you see it for every raid from one faction and want it fixed properly, report this line to the author of the mod that adds that faction or raid strategy.

keywords.li: could not resolve arrival mode for raid

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: raid used a default strategy
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A raid was created without a strategy, so the game fell back to a straightforward immediate attack. The raid still happens; only the tactics the attackers were meant to use were lost.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Nothing is broken and no action is needed. If it repeats, report this line to the author of the mod that triggers that raid or incident.

keywords.li: parms raidstrategy was null but shouldn't be

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a pawn group used a cheap fallback
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: The game could not build the intended group of pawns for a faction at the requested point value, so it spawned a single random cheap group instead. This usually means the faction has no pawn kinds that fit the points or group type - common with modded factions. The event still happens, just with weaker or different pawns than intended.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Nothing is broken - the event went ahead with fallback pawns. If it repeats for one faction, report this line to the author of the mod that adds that faction; its group definitions do not cover this point range.

keywords.li: defaulting to a single random cheap group

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: weather fell back to clear
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: No weather type had a positive chance for the current conditions, so the game defaulted to clear weather. Usually a modded biome or weather mod left no valid weather for this map's situation. The game continues normally.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Nothing is broken. If it repeats on one map, report it to the author of the biome or weather mod - its weather commonalities exclude this map's conditions.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: the error passes through a modified method
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A method in this error's path was replaced at runtime by Harmony, the library mods use to change game behaviour. That is normal - a single mod's patch produces the same frames - and does not by itself mean two mods conflict. It does mean a mod's change is in the code path, and the stack trace can show the original method name even when a mod's rewrite caused the error.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Check the Harmony patch analysis above: it reads the live patch registry and names the actual patching mods. One mod named means update or report to that author; two or more on the same method is a real conflict candidate - disable them one at a time to find the pair.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a UI window threw an error
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A window's draw code threw an exception, so RimWorld closed or skipped the window. A UI panel may vanish or misbehave.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Usually a mod's UI code. Check the likely source and stack trace for the mod, then update or disable it and report the trace to the author.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a per-frame game loop hook threw an error
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A top-level per-frame hook threw, so RimWorld aborted the rest of that frame's drawing (OnGUI) or update logic (Update). Symptoms are often several unrelated UI elements flickering or not updating at once, or the same error repeating every frame.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: A mod running each frame has a bug. Use the stack trace to find it, disable it to confirm, and report the trace. If attribution points only at vanilla, a mod's global draw or update hook is still the likely cause.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a pawn could not reserve its target
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A pawn failed to claim (reserve) the thing it wanted to work on, so the job was cancelled. A burst of these can leave pawns standing idle. With mods that move pawns between maps, it usually means a job aimed at something on a different map.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: If it repeats, the mod driving that job has a targeting bug. Note what the pawns were trying to do, find the mod in the likely source or trace, and report it. A one-off is usually harmless.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a pawn is stuck starting jobs
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A pawn started many jobs in a single tick, which RimWorld stops to avoid a freeze. The pawn's AI is caught in a loop, usually from a mod job or work giver that never completes.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Find the mod behind the job (likely source or trace) and report it. As a workaround, drafting and undrafting the pawn, or removing the mod, breaks the loop.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a job or tick threw an error
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: Code running a pawn's job, or a per-tick update, threw an exception. The pawn may drop the job, freeze, or repeat the error every tick.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: A bug in the mod that owns the job or comp. Use the likely source and trace to find it, then report it or disable it.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: spawn or despawn state error
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: Something tried to spawn a thing that is already in the world, or despawn one that was not, so the world state is inconsistent for that object.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Usually a mod mishandling spawning. Note the thing named and report it with the trace. A single occurrence is often recoverable.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a list changed while it was being read
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: Code changed a collection while another piece of code was looping over it, which throws and aborts whatever was running.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: A threading or ordering bug in the named mod. Report the trace to the author; there is no user-side fix.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: index out of range
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: Code asked for an item past the end of a list or array, so the operation that needed it fails.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: A bug in the named mod, often exposed by another mod changing the data it expected. Report the trace, and try disabling recently added mods.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: invalid cast
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: Code treated an object as a type it is not. In modding this is often a Harmony patch on a generic method firing for the wrong type, which can spam every frame in a window.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Look for the mod in the trace. If it repeats each frame inside a vanilla window, a mod's patch is the cause. Disable suspects one at a time and report the trace.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a lookup key was missing
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: Code looked up a key in a dictionary that did not contain it. This often means a mod's cache was built before all data was ready, or another mod removed something it expected.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: A bug or load-order issue in the named mod. Report the trace. Changing load order or updating the mod sometimes helps.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a bad value was passed to a method
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A method was given an argument it does not accept (null, or out of the allowed range), so it throws instead of continuing.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: A bug in the named mod. Report the trace. If it started after adding a mod, that mod is the likely trigger.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a quest failed to build its text
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A quest could not resolve its description text, usually because a mod quest part left a value unset. The quest may show placeholder text like ERR: or broken tags.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: A bug in the mod that adds that quest. Report it. Declining or ignoring the quest is safe; it will not break your colony.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a def or its components could not be built
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: RimWorld could not create a def from XML, or could not create one of the runtime components a def asks for (a comp, verb, or inspector tab). The item, building, or feature that needed it will be missing or incomplete.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: Usually bad XML or a missing type in the named mod, or a patch conflict. Update the mod, check its dependencies, and report the message if it persists.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: a UI drawing bug
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: A mod's UI code left the text or GUI state wrong at the end of a frame, or mismatched its scroll or group calls. RimWorld reports it once per frame.
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.fix: A drawing bug in the named mod. It is usually cosmetic but can misalign other UI. Report the trace to the author.
